issues.legal_issue: A prior dismissal of an eviction suit on personal-need grounds does not bar a later eviction suit when the later need is different and is assessed as of the later suit’s filing.
material_facts: An earlier eviction suit based on the landlord’s need was dismissed.
The requirement pleaded in the later eviction suit was different from the requirement pleaded in the earlier suit.
The lower courts considered the landlord’s bona fide need with reference to the time the later suit was filed.
issues.conclusion: The earlier dismissal did not bar the later suit, and the courts below were correct to reject the plea of res judicata.
issues.legal_principle: A landlord’s bona fide need is considered with reference to the time the eviction suit is filed; an earlier decision against necessity does not establish that the landlord can never have a genuine need in the future. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited in the judgment.

predicates.eviction_appeal: A party appealed in an eviction proceeding.
predicates.earlier_eviction_suit_dismissed: An earlier eviction suit based on the landlord’s need was dismissed.
predicates.later_requirement_different: The requirement pleaded in the later eviction suit differed from the requirement pleaded in the earlier suit.

issues.definition: When an eviction appeal concerns a later suit based on a requirement different from the one in an earlier dismissed eviction suit, the earlier dismissal does not bar the later suit.

issues.legal_issue: Concurrent findings on the landlord’s need should not be reappraised when there is no reason to disregard them.
material_facts: The lower courts had made concurrent findings on the landlord’s need.
The appellant challenged those findings on the merits.
The Supreme Court found no reason to disregard the findings.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to reappraise the evidence and left the concurrent findings undisturbed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to reappraise concurrent factual findings when it found no reason to ignore them. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited in the judgment.

predicates.civil_appeal: A party brought a civil appeal challenging a lower-court decision.
predicates.concurrent_findings_challenged: The appellant challenged factual findings that the lower courts had made concurrently.
predicates.no_reason_to_disregard_findings: The Court found no reason to disregard the concurrent findings.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal challenges concurrent findings and the Court finds no reason to disregard them, those findings remain undisturbed.

issues.legal_issue: An heir who is allowed to prosecute an appeal on the merits may be treated as substituted despite the absence of a formal substitution order, and the deceased appellant’s widow may also be substituted and heard.
material_facts: The sole appellant died while the appeal was pending.
A son filed an application seeking substitution and claiming the deceased’s estate under an alleged will.
The son was allowed to press the appeal on its merits, although no formal order had been made on the substitution application.
The widow disputed the son’s claim and expressed her desire to challenge the eviction decree.
The Court decided to substitute the widow and permitted her counsel to argue the appeal afresh.
issues.conclusion: The son was deemed to have been substituted because he was allowed to press the appeal, and the Court also substituted the widow and allowed her to argue the appeal afresh.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the son as substituted in substance because he had been allowed to prosecute the appeal, notwithstanding the lack of a formal order; it also decided to substitute the widow and permit a fresh argument. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited in the judgment.

rule.if: appeal_pending_at_appellant_death and heir_substitution_application_filed and heir_permitted_to_press_appeal and widow_seeks_substitution

predicates.appeal_pending_at_appellant_death: The appellant died while an appeal was pending.
predicates.heir_substitution_application_filed: An heir filed an application seeking substitution for the deceased appellant.
predicates.heir_permitted_to_press_appeal: The heir was allowed to argue the appeal on its merits.
predicates.widow_seeks_substitution: The deceased appellant’s widow sought substitution and an opportunity to argue the appeal.

issues.definition: When an appellant dies during a pending appeal, an heir seeks substitution and is allowed to argue, and the widow also seeks substitution and a hearing, the heir is treated as substituted and the widow is substituted and heard.

issues.legal_issue: Appeal notices need not be served on added respondents who have taken no part in the litigation and have not sought substitution or an opportunity to argue.
material_facts: Other heirs were added as respondents after the deceased appellant’s widow was substituted.
Those heirs had taken no interest in the litigation and had not requested substitution or an opportunity to argue the appeal.
The litigation had been pending for many years.
issues.conclusion: It was unnecessary to serve appeal notices on the added respondents.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered service unnecessary in the circumstances where the added respondents had not participated or requested substitution or an opportunity to argue. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited in the judgment.

predicates.appeal_proceeding: An appeal was pending before the Court.
predicates.added_respondents_took_no_part: The added respondents had taken no part in the litigation.
predicates.added_respondents_made_no_request: The added respondents had not requested substitution or an opportunity to argue the appeal.

issues.definition: In an appeal, when added respondents have neither participated nor requested substitution or an opportunity to argue, service of appeal notices is unnecessary.
